targets.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Social Media Use, Big Five Personality, and Well-being.
targets.evidence_quote:
One of the strengths is that this study contributed to the scientific knowledge about screen

time, active and passive social media use, extraversion and life satisfaction by not only

investigating the influencing factors of life satisfaction among university students but also by

targets.outcome_quote:
Regarding the replicated and extended

mediation of the study by Bunz (2021), no indirect effects were found which is in line with the
                                                                                                      32

study by Bunz. Though in the study social media intensity was the mediator between extraversion

and positive well-being, changing the variables to total screen time as a mediator and life

satisfaction as the outcome variable did not yield different results.
targets.outcome_reasoning:
Null mediation agrees with Bunz, but the discussion explicitly contrasts the extraversion–screen time direction: Moreover, as expected, extraversion predicts total screen time, however,

instead of increasing extraversion levels leading to increased screen time, in the current study, the

higher the extraversion level, the less time is spent on screens.

reasoning: Verified thesis title, author, full text and reference list. Bunz is the explicitly replicated original; other citations motivate extensions. No whole-replication verdict overrides the agreement and explicit contrast.
